items.title: Jones Hank — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I met him – – we had a band... Big Nick was, of course, the leader of the band... I enjoyed playing with Nick the short time I played with him.

ctx.x: I once talk specifically about early piano influences like Tatum and Heinz. But, since we digress, I don't want to forget about Big Nick Nicholas.

Right, Big, I met him – – we had a band, it was composed of Howard Brockington, Big Nick, Thad my brother—No, the bass player was Peynton, Lutellis Peynton. He was the one I told you about earlier. Big Nick was, of course, the leader of the band. We, actually didn’t work in Grand Rapids. He came down to the Pontiac area. We worked in…let me think…I think we played one job in Grand Rapids because I remember driving from Pontiac in my car, well, in my father’s car. We drove back in a horrible snowstorm all the way…
Was he fully developed at that time? Was that early on like Lucky Thompson?

Ice to take him down to work in a cab when he had to go to work. I used to meet him and take him down because, as you know, he was legally blind. We developed a friendship. items.title: 67619_Big Nick Nicholas oral history interview
items.q: I met Thad Jones and Hank Jones in Pontiac... Goofus Carnell... got us together... Thad and Hank and then this Howard Brockington... we did a whole summer up there [Idlewilde]

ctx.x: up; who knew you from the early band...?

When I look back, I don't know how this happened...Oh, oh yes I do know how it happened. I met...after I got started playin' pretty good... I met Thad Jones and Hank Jones in Pontiac which was 30 or 35 miles from my home. Goofus Carnell...now it all comes back to me...Goofus Carnell, he took us to... oh, we did some things with Goofus Carnell and he come to Lansing, Michigan, and he had heard about us from somewhere and he said, "Let's do something." So we went up to, one summer, we went up to Idlewilde. We did a…
Were Thad and Hank in the same band?
